search_log: Searched “Circe Madeline Miller official excerpt first chapter publisher,” “Circe Madeline Miller first person narrator point of view interview,” and site-specific author and publisher queries.
Searched “Circe Madeline Miller review first-person narration,” “Circe Madeline Miller chapter one excerpt,” and Google Books preview queries for structural corroboration.
Opened and inspected the authorized BookBrowse Chapter One excerpt, the NEA interview transcript, the Women’s Prize author Q&A, and the Oxford Academic journal article before using them.
A PBS NewsHour result contained an explicit first-person statement in search results but returned HTTP 403 when opened, so it was not used as evidence.

Bloomsbury catalog and Google Books pages supplied bibliographic or promotional material but no useful sustained interior excerpt; research found no credible indication of alternating or non-first-person sections.
person_note: Circe is the participating narrator and tells her own life story in first person. Numerous event quotations independently expose her autobiographical “I,” “me,” and “my”; gnomic statements and direct speech were excluded except where an outside “I said” beat identifies the narrator. The authorized opening, a whole-book scholarly analysis, and two explicit interviews agree, with no evidence of sustained narration in another person. The only material scope limitation is that the Tier A prose source covers the opening, but the whole-book structural sources resolve that limitation.
